_comment: Registry of ANGI install targets. status: 'ready' = builds and boots on hardware; 'experimental' = builds, not yet verified on hardware (installers must say so); 'planned' = no image yet, installers must stop and never substitute another board's image.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi 5
boards.how_to_tell: Two micro-HDMI ports, a USB-C power port, a power button, a fan connector, and a full-size Ethernet port. 'Raspberry Pi 5' is printed on the board.

marketing.tagline: The fastest Pi, with the full desktop.
marketing.card: A microSD card of 16 GB or more (32 GB tested). Your agent formats it for you; everything on it is erased.
marketing.reader: Put the card in a card reader on your computer. Leave the Pi off with its card slot empty.
marketing.connect: Your agent tells you when to put the finished card in the Pi and connect an Ethernet cable or a USB-C data cable.

install.connection: Use a suitable Pi 5 power supply with direct Ethernet, or use a USB-C data connection with adequate power.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi 4 / 400 / CM4
boards.dt_model: Raspberry Pi 4|Raspberry Pi 400|Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4
boards.how_to_tell: Two micro-HDMI ports, a USB-C power port, no power button, and a full-size Ethernet port. 'Raspberry Pi 4' is printed on the board.
boards.note: Includes ANGI Desktop, VNC over SSH, and ANGI Web. Desktop and browser hardware verification is pending.

marketing.card: A microSD card of 16 GB or more (32 GB works well). Your agent formats it for you; everything on it is erased.
marketing.reader: Put the card in a card reader on your computer. Leave the Pi off with its card slot empty.
marketing.connect: Your agent tells you when to put the finished card in the Pi, power it with a 5 V / 3 A supply, and connect an Ethernet cable or a USB-C data cable.

install.connection: Use a suitable Pi 4 power supply with direct Ethernet, or use a USB-C data connection with adequate power.

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
boards.note: The source build selects the software VNC desktop. Boot and desktop verification on the Zero 2 W are pending.
boards.how_to_tell: Tiny board, one mini-HDMI port, no Ethernet port, 'Zero 2 W' printed on it.

marketing.card: A microSD card of 16 GB or more. Your agent formats it for you; everything on it is erased.
marketing.reader: Put the card in a card reader on your computer. Leave the Pi off and empty.
marketing.connect: Your agent guides you through setup over the micro-USB data port. The Zero 2 W reaches the internet over 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.

install.connection: Use the micro-USB port marked USB for the headless data connection. Use the separate PWR IN port if the workstation cannot reliably supply power. Use 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi.

boards.name: ARM desktop or laptop (UEFI)
boards.medium: USB stick or SD card in a USB reader
boards.how_to_tell: A normal computer with a UEFI/BIOS that is not x86 (for example Ampere, Apple-silicon VMs, Snapdragon X).

marketing.card: An SD card or USB drive of 16 GB or more. Your agent formats it for you; everything on it is erased.
marketing.reader: Plug the drive or card reader into the computer you are working on, not the one ANGI is going on.
marketing.connect: Your agent tells you when to plug the finished drive into your ARM computer and start it from that drive.

install.connection: Power the target normally and choose the USB stick or USB SD card reader in its 64-bit UEFI boot menu.

boards.note: Source configuration available. Physical boot, networking, and USB-reader verification are pending.

boards.name: x86-64 desktop or laptop (UEFI)
boards.medium: USB stick or SD card in a USB reader
boards.how_to_tell: A normal Intel or AMD computer.

marketing.card: An SD card or USB drive of 16 GB or more. Your agent formats it for you; everything on it is erased.
marketing.reader: Plug the drive or card reader into the computer you are working on, not the one ANGI is going on.
marketing.connect: Your agent tells you when to plug the finished drive into your Intel or AMD computer and start it from that drive.

install.connection: Power the target normally and choose the USB stick or USB SD card reader in its 64-bit UEFI boot menu.

boards.note: Source configuration available. Physical boot, networking, and USB-reader verification are pending.
